### D.5 Tremor (`tremor_offset`)

The tremor offset formula is defined as:

`s(t) = 0.6 * sin(2 * pi * f1 * t + phi1) + 0.4 * sin(2 * pi * f2 * t + phi2)`, `t = present_time`; `f_1 = 6.0 + 1.5 * u_1` (6.0 .. 7.5 Hz) and `f_2 = 9.0 + 1.0 * u_2` (9.0 .. 10.0 Hz), two **disjoint sub-bands** of the 6-10 Hz tremor band, so `f_2 - f_1` >= 1.5 Hz and the beat period is at most 0.67 s *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (the earlier shared band let about 12 % of instruments draw near-equal frequencies and so long or permanent null windows with no tremor); `(u_i, phi_i)` from a presentation-local stateless hash of `(ref_key, i)`

`A_eff = max( TREMOR_AMP_PX, ceil( TREMOR_MIN_SCREEN_PX / k ) )`

`env(t) = min(1, (t - t_on) / TREMOR_ONSET_MS)` while `p_eff` holds; `env_off x max(0, 1 - (t - t_off) / TREMOR_DECAY_MS)` after it ends, with `env_off` = `env(t_off)` **latched at the instant the predicate ends** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (the earlier decay branch started from 1.0, so a predicate pulse that ended mid-onset jumped the envelope up to full before decaying); `p_eff = predicate OR (t - t_last_true) < TREMOR_HOLD_S`

`o = clamp( round( TREMOR_GAIN * A_eff * env * s(t) * tremor_weight_pm / 1000 ), -A_eff, +A_eff )` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: `tremor_weight_pm` factor, PF-8, PF-17)*. **State at lie onset** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*: in every HONEST frame `tremor_weight_pm` = 1000, so every existing HONEST number is unchanged; in a non-HONEST frame `env` = `env_hold` (the env of the last HONEST frame, latched at the first non-HONEST frame; 0 if no tremor was running; the predicate is not read and env neither rises nor decays), so the weight alone carries the fade. The offset is **in frame-index space** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `o` is a number of pre-rendered needle frames (OQ-IW-7: one frame index is one tip pixel along the arc, or one meniscus row of a LINEAR glass), and the drawn index is `idx_drawn = clamp( idx_base + o, 0, N_idx - 1 )` with `idx_base` the settle or ramp base index and `N_idx` the frame count of the sheet, so a non-zero `o` always moves the drawn tip by exactly `o` indices (the earlier tangent offset in art px could round to the same tip pixel on about 9 % of frames at 45 degrees) and the sum can never leave the end stops. The angular equivalent is `o x arc_deg / (N_idx - 1)` degrees

(The two-sine sum is wanted here: PF D.4 rejected it for the **wander** because a beat that dips to rest would break never-rest, whereas tremor has no never-rest duty and its irregularity is the point; a dip to rest between bursts reads as a real needle on a shaking hull.)

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TREMOR_F_MIN_HZ`, `TREMOR_F_MAX_HZ` | float Hz | 6 and 10 (named here from ART 7.3, not new) | art bible | the tremor band; disjoint from the Filter's 0.40-0.45 Hz wander; the two sines draw from the sub-bands 6.0-7.5 and 9.0-10.0 Hz inside it | *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*
| `u_i`, `phi_i` | float | [0, 1), [0, 2 pi) | a presentation hash of `ref_key` (PF D.14 is the precedent; ADR candidate); **never** the kernel `rng_derive`, sim RNG is never used for presentation | per-instrument frequencies and phases, so two trembling gauges do not move in step |
| `TREMOR_AMP_PX` | int art px | 1 (ART 7.3 +-1), range 1-2 | this GDD | amplitude in art px |
| `TREMOR_MIN_SCREEN_PX` | int screen px | 2 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 2-3 | this GDD | the HR-12 floor applied to tremor |
| `k` | int | 1..`k_auto`+2 | PIPE zoom ladder | world scale |
| `TREMOR_GAIN` | float | 1.5 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 1.2-2.0 | this GDD | gain per unit of `A_eff` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: at `A_eff` 1, abs(o) = 1 when abs(s) >= 0.33; at `A_eff` 2, abs(o) = 1 when abs(s) >= 0.167 and 2 when abs(s) >= 0.5 |
| `TREMOR_ONSET_MS`, `TREMOR_DECAY_MS` | int ms | 150 (100-300), 600 (300-1000) `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | envelope; on a re-rise during a decay `t_on := t - env x TREMOR_ONSET_MS` so `env` stays continuous |
| `TREMOR_HOLD_S` | float s | 0 (range 0-1.0) `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | the playtest remedy if the predicate flaps at Graph-step rate |
| `predicate` | bool | | IW-12, refreshed per Graph step | true only while `motion_mode` is HONEST and a physical stress cause holds; not read in a non-HONEST frame (`env_hold` stands) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* |
| `tremor_weight_pm` | int per mille | 0..1000 | `Perceived` (PF-8), Filter-owned, not a knob | 1000 on the honest path; from a lie's first ACTIVE frame falls linearly to 0 over `TREMOR_BLEND_S`; stays 0 until CLEAR *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* |
| `TREMOR_BLEND_S` | float s | 1.0 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, := `WANDER_ONSET_S` (range 0.5-3.0) | Filter (cited, not owned) | the fade window *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* |

## Acceptance Criteria

*All criteria are GIVEN / WHEN / THEN and ids are `AC-IW-n` (the numbering was kept stable through the QA review, so the groups below are by topic, not contiguous). **Tags.** (auto) an automated test, logic in `tests/unit/instruments/`, integration in `tests/integration/instruments/`; (lint) a build or content lint (instrument data, scene tree, sheets, scripts); (review) a design or lead review of a document or a retained screenshot; (manual) a playtest or a retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/`; (spike) a time-boxed engine test whose result may change the design. `(provisional — X)` marks a criterion that depends on a neighbour still being written or a reply owed. **Test-evidence gate.** This is a UI plus Visual / Feel system: every criterion that cites a retained screenshot (AC-IW-5, 9, 25, 29, 48, 100 and the screenshot legs of 1 and 6) is BLOCKING at every `qa.level` including `minimal` (coding standards: a parse check is not a run); Logic criteria (D.1 to D.6, D.8 to D.12, IW-5, IW-11 to IW-14, IW-17, IW-19, IW-21, IW-24) need files in `tests/unit/instruments/`; the card joins with the Filter, Interaction and the Controller are Integration. **No criterion asserts that the indicative IW-29 manifest passes floor (i)** (advisor ruling R17). **Conventions fixed for every vector:** `round` is half away from zero, a "rolling second" is [t, t + 1000 ms), and a **tip-pixel flip** is a frame whose rounded tip coordinate differs from the previous frame's (Formulas intro, D.3, VA-6).*

**Conventions for the criteria below** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. (1) **Latency oracle.** One convention for AC-IW-33, AC-IW-91 and AC-IW-114: a latency is counted in render frames at a fixed 60 Hz test clock between the frame in which the Adapter receives the cause and the first frame whose draw list reflects it. "Closed in the same render frame" means the instrument's probe `is_card_open()` reads false (and the card root's `visible` is false) by the end of that frame's `_process`; Godot's `queue_free()` runs at the end of the frame, so the test asserts the probe in the same frame and `is_instance_valid(card)` false at the start of the next frame, and never asserts node validity inside the frame of the cause. "Opens on the next render frame" means `is_card_open()` reads true at the end of the frame after the press. (2) **Seeds.** Every randomised test takes its seeds from a fixed list in the test data and prints them; no wall clock, no unseeded RNG. (3) **Machine.** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12, which closes X14 and supersedes R11)* A performance criterion is gated on the two reference machines at the spike: RM-DESKTOP (Windows 10/11 64-bit; 6-core/6-thread CPU of the Intel Core i5-9400F / AMD Ryzen 5 2600 class; 8 GB RAM; GPU of the NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti 4 GB / AMD Radeon RX 570 4 GB class, Vulkan 1.2+; SATA SSD; 1920x1080 at 60 Hz; P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 16.6 ms) and RM-DECK (Steam Deck LCD 2022, SteamOS stable, 1280x800 at 60 Hz panel, 30 fps target; P99 ceiling 33.3 ms); `project.yaml` `qa.min_spec` records both. Every wall-clock figure is taken on a release export (Godot 4.7.2 release export template, not the editor and not a debug template), renderer `forward_plus`, vsync on, after the pipeline's 120-frame warm-up, with the startup read-back (renderer, driver) recorded with each result; a pass needs P99 at most 90 % of the ceiling (headroom at least 1.7 ms desktop, 3.3 ms Deck). A figure not yet measured is "pending spike measurement on RM-DESKTOP / RM-DECK", not blocked. The CI runner (its description recorded in the output) and the developer's machine give indicative figures only. (4) **Playtest coding rule.** For every (manual) playtest criterion the protocol is a scripted session, the observed statement is the tester's first unprompted explanation, it is coded by two coders against the criterion's word list (or the codes named in the criterion), a disagreement is settled by the producer, and the raw codes are retained in `production/qa/evidence/`.

content.content:
### D.1b bead_segments *(added 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D39, default applied confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20))*

The bead_segments formula is defined as:

`bead_segments(h) = clamp(1 + floor(2 * (h - LEAK_HP) / (PATCH_CAP_BP - LEAK_HP)), 1, 3)`, where `h` is the patched subject's true `hp`, read live by the Module-Body Presenter (In-World Instruments IW-18) through the Graph's LS-19 `node_hp(id)` (the `hp` field of `edge(id)` for an edge). For the whole `PATCH_DECAY_S` 240 s hold `h` equals the banked hp at the end of the patch, completed or cancelled; after the hold it falls with the Graph's wear (100 bp per 10 s) and the bead shortens. Interaction never reads it, never in `validate` (IA-11a), and calls no mutator. The bead is drawn on the patch plate (module-body, IW-18), not by Failure & Trail: FT-32's `27 PATCH_WEEP` is one static POINT_FIXED mark per medium with no length axis and is identical for all three bead lengths. Checks at registry defaults (`LEAK_HP` 4000, `PATCH_CAP_BP` 6000, span 2000): `h` 4000 → 1 + floor(0) = 1; 4999 → 2 × 999 / 2000 = 0.999 → 1 + 0 = 1; 5000 → 1 + floor(1) = 2; 5999 → 2 × 1999 / 2000 = 1.999 → 1 + 1 = 2; 6000 → 1 + floor(2) = 3; after the first wear tick, 5900 → 2 × 1900 / 2000 = 1.9 → 1 + 1 = 2. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `h` | int bp | 4000..6000 for a patched subject (a cancel before the first block leaves `h` unchanged) | the Graph's true `hp` | banked hp when the patch ended |
| `LEAK_HP` | int bp | 4000 | registry (cited) | hp at which the LEAK clears |
| `PATCH_CAP_BP` | int bp | 6000 | registry (cited) | the PATCH ceiling |
| `PATCH_DECAY_S` | int s | 240 | registry (cited) | the Graph's hold before wear (LS-23) |
| wear rate | bp per s | 10 (100 bp per 10 s) | Graph LS-23 (cited) | decay after the hold |

======
**IW-18. WORN and patched presentation.**
*Rule.* A WORN subject (DEGRADED, no hazard mode, `medium` NONE, `acoustic` NONE; LS-11) shows module-body wear: the wear overlay frame (scuffs, and a visible patch plate if patched) on the machine and on the instrument bound to it; the gauge shows the perceived reading of the module's output as usual. No word, bar, rating, colour grade or numeral says "worn" (BS-6, IA-39). A patched subject is permanently DEGRADED `sev` 1 (LS-10, D.4) and keeps its patch plate; the plate is driven by the node's patched state (`hp_cap < HP_FULL`; the Graph's PATCH_WEEP id 27 row uses the same condition and draws the weep on the consequence channel, which Instruments never touch) and not by the WORN descriptor *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Failure & Trail draws nothing for WORN (FT:232, :637). The wear overlay is corruptible only through the machine-frame swap at stage 3 (a false-fixed scrubber looks whole while its witness says otherwise); it is honest at stages 0-2. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6 GAP: the Module-Body Presenter owns the patch plate, so it gains the D39 bead axis that Interaction D.1b needs and that Failure & Trail cannot draw, FT-32 row 27 being one static POINT_FIXED mark with no length axis.)* **Patch-plate bead.** The patch plate carries a weld bead of 1, 2 or 3 segments (user-confirmed default D39, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20); registry `bead_segments`, owner Interaction D.1b): the Presenter selects one of three bead frames of the plate overlay by `bead_segments(h) = clamp(1 + floor(2 * (h - LEAK_HP) / (PATCH_CAP_BP - LEAK_HP)), 1, 3)` with h = the subject's true `hp` from the Graph (LS-19: `node_hp(id)`, or the `hp` field of `edge(id)` for an edge). At registry defaults (`LEAK_HP` 4000, `PATCH_CAP_BP` 6000, span 2000): hp 4000-4999 gives 1, 5000-5999 gives 2, 6000 gives 3. h equals the banked hp at the end of the patch for the whole `PATCH_DECAY_S` 240 s hold, then falls with the wear (100 bp per 10 s: 5900 gives 2), so the bead shortens as the patch wears. The bead is the only thing that varies between the three frames: no numeral, word, colour change or overlay (BS-6, IA-39, AD-14). The hp read is made in the same per-step non-value read as the frame selection (IW-5), so the AC-IW-62 read count is unchanged and nothing is read per frame. Frames: three bead frames of the patch-plate overlay (`ovl_patch_<loop>_alb`), authored once per module sheet, inside the P0 "WORN overlay and patch plate" row. The plate and bead are drawn from the patched state (`hp_cap < HP_FULL`), stay drawn under a stage-3 swap (E-IW-38) and are removed by a FULL repair (`hp_cap` back to `HP_FULL`). The patched-not-cured tell on the consequence channel is the Graph's `27 PATCH_WEEP` weep, which this system never touches.
*Why.* Routed thread 5; BS-6 and IA-39: no condition surface.
*Edge notes.* Wear frames are authored once per module sheet, never per loose item (AD-BS-5 forbids a per-loose-item wear set as "the inspect card in disguise"). WORN is shown here on module-body surfaces only; the card shows no wear (IW-22). LS-11 (mode 10 WORN: "readable on the sprite, the gauge and the inspect card") and LSG:168 are read as: WORN reaches the card only through the module's reduced output reading; the card carries no wear frame, word or mark (advisor ruling R2).

**IW-19. The in-world alarm mark: TRUTH-graded, on the housing, alarm-eligible only.**
*Rule.* While the bound subject has an `alarm_eligible` failure descriptor (LS-13; severity >= 3; read through `failures(filter)`), an instrument housing that can carry it shows one Alarm Red `#E0102A` chamfered-square warning mark (ART:817 shape, ART 7.2 canonical size 16x16 art px, `ALARM_MARK_WORLD_PX` 16, "nothing smaller") on the **housing, not the face**. The world twin's exclamation stroke is **Void Steel**, not Paper White (Paper White is UI-only, fact 16, ART 4.6; the HUD twin keeps Paper White). **Where the mark may be drawn (stage-12 CD-GDD-ALIGN concern 1, P4 cost rule; rewritten 2026-10-27 as a decision table).** The mark is drawn only on a housing that is physically at the alarm-eligible subject. That is a property of placement data (`mount_room`, `subject_room`, `host_node`, IW-8) and not of a tag: the decision table below lists every case. An instrument with `hops(mount_room, subject_room)` >= 1 (REMOTE) satisfies none of the yes rows, so the lethal remote FALSE_OK of Beat C is never put beside its own contradiction by a lit Alarm Red mark on the lying instrument's housing, and believing the mark still costs a walk to where the subject is (P4: checking costs time, risk or trust). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The mark itself stays TRUTH-graded and untagged; this rule decides only on which housings it is drawn, from authored placement data (`mount_room`, `subject_room`, `host_node` and the binding), never from a lie state. The mark lives on a DIAL_L housing meeting that test (in the 36 px horizontal bay beside the 60x46 housing), on machine and console panels and on the tank prop meeting it; **DIAL_S carries none** *(orchestrator ruling: the art-director's narrowing adopted over the ux-designer's 4-row overlap of the DIAL_S arc; a 16x16 mark cannot sit on a 46x35 housing in a 48x48 cell; K-15 is therefore reframed from "overlap" to "which housings carry the mark", route art-director; the DIAL_S instrument's consequence-channel hiss, draught and sweep are its alarm)*. It is an **untagged node** (PF-4 default TRUTH), separate from every corruptible ref, so no HOUSING_GLOW or MACHINE_FRAME lie can add, move or suppress it; it is a witness and never itself a lying surface (SN L-A, SN:262). It never appears as the first warning (`alarm_eligible` is the only state in which an alarm-class presentation may play, and `W_MIN_WARNING_S` 10 guarantees a prior tell on endogenous transitions). `alarm_eligible` is a field of the `FailureDescriptor` (LS-14) that also requires the fairness gate to be open: Instruments **never re-derive it from `sev`**. The mark pulses in the beacon rhythm (2-3 s period, never faster than 3 Hz, HR-13; ART 7.3), holds solid under reduced motion, is non-emissive, casts no light and is lit-gated by the renderer like the housing. The needle and zones keep showing the perceived reading. The card does not carry the mark. **Decoupling rule (so the mark is never a free falsifier):** a zone's onset (an LS-7 band edge) and `alarm_eligible` (`sev` >= 3) are different quantities and do not coincide; **the absence of the mark never proves a needle in an alarm zone is lying** (the rule is one-directional: absence is never evidence; presence is the ship speaking and outranks the needle, E-IW-37), and a lying FALSE_FAIL needle in an alarm zone without a mark is not distinguishable from a true reading approaching alarm on that evidence alone (advisor ruling R14; K-8).
*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **IW-19 decision table (housing, mount, binding, `hops`).** A mark also requires an `alarm_eligible` descriptor on the bound subject (above); the table decides only whether the housing may carry one.

### Gaps / untestable as written

1. **AC-IW-55 is BLOCKED, not passing.** The presenter CPU budget has no owner number (OQ-IW-10); until the technical-director sets one the criterion can be run and recorded but not passed or failed.
2. **AC-IW-70's emission leg is BLOCKED** until the Lighting spike sets `PIP_EMIT_MAX` (ART 8.12); the presence / absence leg is testable now.

**DO-22. Render-probe: an optional input.** *Rule:* The Overlay asks In-World Instruments (designed (this run); P-2, accepted by IW-38) for a dev-only `drawn_value(ref)` per corruptible node: the displayed value the node actually drew this frame, as the **pre-snap needle angle in integer millidegrees** (the angle before the pixel snap, so a snapped drawn angle is never compared with an unsnapped perceived one), and a dev-only `drawn_leak(ref)`: the gleam amplitude actually drawn this frame, per mille (DO-21 row 3; both asks go to the Instruments owner with the accepted IW-38 probe, OQ-DO-26). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* When present, the class `DEFECT_BYPASS` (the drawn angle differs from the angle implied by `p.displayed_pm` by more than `LEAK_EPS_MDEG` = `LEAK_EPS_DEG` x 1000 = 250 millidegrees, compared as integers and inclusive: exactly 250 passes) detects a node that skipped the Filter. When absent, the classifier stops at `perceived` versus `true_value` versus ledger, and the row's `bypass_check` field reads `ABSENT`; it is never shown as clean and the row's class is not changed to `UNAVAILABLE` on that account alone. The same holds for an absent `drawn_leak(ref)` and the row's `leak_check` field. A ref whose calibration has `value_hi <= value_lo` or `arc_deg <= 0` cannot be mapped to an angle or a grid: it classifies `UNAVAILABLE` / `NO_RESOLVER` and never reaches a probe verdict. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(accepted by Instruments IW-38; until the probe is live in a build, `bypass_check` reads `ABSENT`.)* *Why:* a node that bypasses the Filter looks exactly like a defect and is invisible without the probe; and this is the only place `LEAK_EPS_DEG` is used (it is a needle-angle epsilon in degrees, not a quantum for mGU, mC, dkPa, permille or bp). *AC group:* classifier.
- **AC-IW-46** (auto, plus lint) [IW-38]: (auto) GIVEN a dev build, WHEN `drawn_value(ref)` is read, THEN it equals what was drawn; `ref_key` is a stable integer, unique per instrument and identical across a restore; `instrument_diag` returns exactly {`instrument_id`, `ref_key`, `motion_mode` as drawn, `settle_active`, `tremor_active`, `card_open`, `state`}; neither probe returns `true_value`. (lint) a release build contains no `drawn_value` or `instrument_diag` symbol and the Overlay treats an absent probe as `bypass_check: ABSENT`, never clean (DO-22). - **If both the bound node's own hazard-mode descriptor (predicate i) and a cable overload (predicate ii) hold**: the predicate is their OR and there is one tremor with one envelope; stress sources are never summed into a larger amplitude. (E-IW-13)
- **If the bound node becomes DESTROYED, SALVAGED or ABSENT while the card is open**: the card closes that frame and the wall node shows the DEAD frame (hairline crack, 4-px needle stub), with no prompt, card, gleam, tremor or pip. A gauge that vanished would read as a bug and one that kept reading would assert a reading from a destroyed thing. (E-IW-20)
- **If the stress predicate holds while the reading is lying**: no NEW tremor and no notch are drawn (the predicate is not read in a non-HONEST frame, and the notch clears at once); a tremor already running at onset fades out over `TREMOR_BLEND_S` (D.5) and the needle is then still of its own accord but never at rest, because the Filter's wander has faded in over the same window; the lie carries its own gleam, never-rest motion and sound (HR-5). The absence of a tremor after the fade is therefore not an oracle, and neither is a tremor that fades during the first second of a lie, because the lie is separately detectable by all three modes. (E-IW-35) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*
- **If the kernel restores while a tremor predicate still holds**: the tremor restarts from its onset ramp (`TREMOR_ONSET_MS`), because the presentation envelope is reset by `hard_start`; the player may see the shake begin again, which is true to the cause. (E-IW-41)

findings.section: Formulas D.5 Output Range, AC-IW-51, OQ-IW-41 (vs perception-filter.md WANDER_AMP_PX L769)

findings.section: IW-38 / instrument_diag vs debug-overlay-true-values.md DO-22 (and AC-IW-46)
findings.finding: Interface mismatch for the dev-only render probe. DO-22 defines `drawn_value(ref)` as the pre-snap needle angle in integer millidegrees. It flags DEFECT_BYPASS when the drawn angle differs from the angle implied by `displayed_pm` by more than 250 mdeg (about 1 pm). IW-38 and AC-IW-46 define `drawn_value` only as 'the value it actually drew', with no unit and no statement of whether it includes the honest ramp lag, the settle, or the tremor offset. The tremor offset is added in frame-index space, one index per tip pixel (about 10-13 pm, 2.4-3.2 deg). The honest ramp lags by up to 16.7 pm (about 4 deg). Settle overshoot is larger still. findings.fix: In IW-38 and AC-IW-46, define `drawn_value(ref)` as the Filter-driven base before presentation-local offsets: `displayed_pm` converted to millidegrees, before ramp, settle, tremor and pixel snap. Give the unit explicitly. Add a separate `drawn_tip_index` field if the Overlay wants the post-snap value. Add an AC where a running honest tremor, ramp and settle all read as not BYPASS. Route the same wording to DO-22.

findings.section: IW-32, AC-IW-45 vs AC-IW-123, IW-24 (and adaptive-audio-and-tells.md L187, L1181)

findings.section: IW-9, IW-5, OQ-IW-20, AC-IW-63 (vs life-support-graph.md L252)
findings.finding: The cross-GDD conflict on `load` is not fixed. findings.fix: Have the Graph writer replace L252's 'its own reading' with a published `load_pm` true_value kind (0 when supply is 0, else min(1250, floor(1000 x demand / supply)), quantum LOAD_QUANTUM_PERMILLE 20). findings.section: Formulas D.5 Output Range, AC-IW-51, OQ-IW-41 (vs perception-filter.md WANDER_AMP_PX L769)
findings.finding: The stale wander figure is still in the file. D.5 says 'wander peaks at 2 art px at 0.35-0.45 Hz ... At k 1 the peaks are equal (2 art px)'. AC-IW-51 says '2 art px peak, 0.35-0.45 Hz', and OQ-IW-41 says the two 'share a 2 art px peak'. The Filter's registered WANDER_AMP_PX is 2.2 art px with f 0.40-0.45 Hz, which this file already quotes correctly in Feel L1599 and the Tuning table. The 'equal peaks' sentence is false (2.2 vs 2), and the tremor-vs-wander cue argument at k 1 rests on it. The new fade text in D.5 sits right next to this sentence.
findings.fix: Replace '2 art px at 0.35-0.45 Hz' with '2.2 art px at 0.40-0.45 Hz' in D.5 L788, AC-IW-51 and OQ-IW-41. Change 'the peaks are equal' to 'the peaks are within 0.2 px (2.2 vs 2)'. Also fix the ±2 px wander wording at VA-6 L1423 if it is meant as the Filter's value.

findings.section: IW-38 / instrument_diag vs debug-overlay-true-values.md DO-22 (and AC-IW-46)
findings.finding: Interface mismatch for the dev-only render probe. DO-22 defines `drawn_value(ref)` as the pre-snap needle angle in integer millidegrees. It flags DEFECT_BYPASS when the drawn angle differs from the angle implied by `displayed_pm` by more than 250 mdeg (about 1 pm). IW-38 and AC-IW-46 define `drawn_value` only as 'the value it actually drew', with no unit and no statement of whether it includes the honest ramp lag, the settle, or the tremor offset. The tremor offset is added in frame-index space, one index per tip pixel (about 10-13 pm, 2.4-3.2 deg). The honest ramp lags by up to 16.7 pm (about 4 deg). Settle overshoot is larger still. If `drawn_value` includes any of these, every honest ramp, settle or tremor, including the new tremor fade, would classify as DEFECT_BYPASS. This pass added only a note that a non-HONEST mode with tremor_active is not a defect. It did not fix the probe's definition.
findings.fix: In IW-38 and AC-IW-46, define `drawn_value(ref)` as the Filter-driven base before presentation-local offsets: `displayed_pm` converted to millidegrees, before ramp, settle, tremor and pixel snap. Give the unit explicitly. Add a separate `drawn_tip_index` field if the Overlay wants the post-snap value. Add an AC where a running honest tremor, ramp and settle all read as not BYPASS. Route the same wording to DO-22.

findings.section: IW-32, AC-IW-45 vs AC-IW-123, IW-24 (and adaptive-audio-and-tells.md L187, L1181)
findings.finding: AC-IW-45 still says instruments publish 'only the presentation signals card_opened and card_closed'. IW-24, E-IW-20 and AC-IW-123 require a distinct unlatch request (`UI_INSTRUMENT_CARD_UNLATCH`) on a light-loss close. A correct build therefore fails AC-IW-45. Adaptive Audio's UI-bus list (L187, L1181) names only OPEN and CLOSE, so the unlatch event has no consumer or owner.
findings.fix: Rewrite AC-IW-45 as: 'publishes only card_opened, card_closed and card_unlatched (the light-loss close) and requests no sound directly'. Add the signal and its UI_INSTRUMENT_CARD_UNLATCH event to the Audio event list (owner-adds, G6 GAP), or remove the unlatch cue from IW-24.

findings.section: IW-24, IW-33, E-IW-25/60, AC-IW-40, AC-IW-114 (vs player-controller-input.md L102, L108-112)
findings.finding: The Controller's context return table makes Esc from `inspect_card` close the card first, with 'no pause and no overlay opens on that press'. A pause can only start from `gameplay`, where the card is already closed. AC-IW-40 ('card open ... the kernel pauses ... the card is closed in the same render frame') and AC-IW-114 ('context becomes chart_table (pause)') cannot be set up through the Adapter. The pause-closes-card behaviour only exists for a kernel-forced pause, such as a lost-focus or system pause, and that source is not named.
findings.fix: Re-word the S4 rows and ACs so the close is caused by Esc/`chart_table` (card closes first) or by a named forced-pause source. Test a kernel-forced pause with a stub that bypasses the Adapter, and say so. Drop the 'context becomes chart_table (pause)' leg.

findings.section: IW-9, IW-5, OQ-IW-20, AC-IW-63 (vs life-support-graph.md L252)
findings.finding: The cross-GDD conflict on `load` is not fixed. LSG L252 still says 'Instruments' load = floor(1000 x demand / max(1, supply)) is its own reading, not rho, and reads no cap', and the Graph has no load_pm (0 hits). Instruments may not read true values; only the Filter calls true_value. The Graph's text therefore describes an unimplementable path. `load` is the only settle_eligible quantity, so the honest heavy-settle signature (the Fantasy's detent plus heavy ease) depends on this. G2 already records the grant of load_pm, or the Filter-derived wrap, as a pre-VS gate. G6 says a GAP is fixed by the owner adding the surface.
findings.fix: Have the Graph writer replace L252's 'its own reading' with a published `load_pm` true_value kind (0 when supply is 0, else min(1250, floor(1000 x demand / supply)), quantum LOAD_QUANTUM_PERMILLE 20). Otherwise add the Filter-derived wrap statement. The Fantasy sentence about the settle must be re-worded to the detent-only signature if neither lands before VS (G2).

findings.section: Player Fantasy L149 vs AC-IW-52
findings.finding: AC-IW-52 still has a numeric pass line: 'no player opens it on more than 50 % of the instruments they pass lit'. The Fantasy says there is no pass line on spam, and the creative-director concurred earlier that spamming the card is harmless by design. The criterion fails a build for behaviour the Fantasy declares acceptable.
findings.fix: Drop the 50 % clause from AC-IW-52, or demote it to a recorded, non-gating observation ('record opens per lit instrument; no pass line').

findings.finding: The bead feature added this pass is not carried through the asset list. IW-18 names three bead frames of `ovl_patch_<loop>_alb`. VA-11 lists `mach_patch_plate_<size>_alb.png` (s 16, m 24, l 32) with no bead frames and no `<loop>` axis. AC-IW-98 checks only P0 asset existence by VA-11 names, so the three frames cannot be verified. AC-IW-29's bead leg tests selection (frame index) but not that three distinct frames exist or that they differ only in the bead (the 'differ in nothing else' claim).
findings.fix: Change the VA-11 row to `mach_patch_plate_<size>_bead<1..3>_alb.png` (or one sheet with 3 frames), drop the `<loop>` axis, and use one name in IW-18. Add a lint or diff leg to AC-98/AC-29: the three frames differ only inside the bead region.

findings.section: Tuning Knobs preamble / D.4 L721 / T_VIS_MAX_S row
findings.finding: Unchanged. D.4 L721 still defines `t_s(2%) = 4/(zeta*omega)`, the approximation that AC-IW-16 and AC-IW-87 explicitly say is NOT asserted (the exact 2 % time is 299 ms; the 4/(zeta*omega) value is 286 ms). findings.section: IW-13 BREATH row / AC-IW-19 BREATH leg vs perception-filter.md PF-19
findings.finding: The BREATH row says `frame_override` is 'drawn and held still for the whole lie', and the AC-IW-19 BREATH leg asserts the drawn frame equals `frame_override` for 12 s. PF-19 gives SPRITE_SWAP a 'gleam-leads-cut onset', so `frame_override` may be NONE for the first frames of the lie while the gleam leads. Instruments should draw the honest frame until the cut. As written, the AC contradicts the Filter's staged onset for the first frames.
findings.fix: Re-word to 'once `frame_override` is non-NONE, the drawn frame is `frame_override` and never changes until CLEAR; while NONE the honest frame is drawn'. Run the 12 s window from the first non-NONE frame.

findings.finding: The new sentence 'the needle is then still of its own accord but never at rest, because the Filter's wander has faded in' is self-contradictory. A needle with wander is not 'still'.
findings.fix: Replace with 'the tremor is then 0, and the needle keeps moving on the Filter's wander and glide, so it is never at rest'.
